  • Work under tight deadlines in a high-volume, fast-paced environment
  • Source candidates across LATAM using job boards, social media, referrals, and direct outreach
  • Coordinate interviews and manage communication between candidates and hiring teams
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date records in the applicant tracking system (ATS)
  • Ensure compliance with healthcare staffing regulations and internal policies
  • Build and maintain a strong pipeline of qualified candidates

Requirements

  • Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish required

Please note that this is a full-time contractor position (40 hours per week) with a negotiable pay rate depending on skillset and experience. The schedule is Monday through Friday, from 8 AM to 4 PM PST.

raw.description:
AI Growth Marketer to own Livaclean's Shopify DTC channel — build landing pages with Claude CLI, create static ad variations at scale, and run A/B tests across the funnel. Livaclean is a 7-year-old ecommerce skincare brand (pimple patches, face care, hair care) with a fully remote team across Pakistan, Philippines, India, and LATAM.

The Role

We're a 95% Amazon business building our DTC/Shopify channel (~$25K/month today). This is an experimental, builder-stage role you're not maintaining a system, you're creating one. Claude CLI proficiency is a hard requirement.

You'll own the static ad pipeline: produce 20-50 AI-powered ad variations/week, test messaging across awareness levels, and feed winning data to our video creative team. 500+ UGC videos/month already flowing in for creative mining.

What You'll Do

Build and optimize Shopify landing pages, PDPs, and advertorials using Claude CLI (~30%)

Create 20-50 static ad variations/week using AI tools — test hooks across problem/solution/product-aware audiences (~30%)

Run A/B tests across pages, ads, and email — track CTR, CPA, ROAS, and conversion rates (~20%)

Optimize Klaviyo email flows (welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase) (~10%)

Develop ad concepts at volume, mine UGC library, collaborate with Creative Lead (~10%)

Requirements

Must-Have:

Claude CLI proficiency (this is non-negotiable)

Marketing fundamentals: awareness levels, funnels, A/B testing, ad performance analysis

Shopify experience (PDP editing, DTC ecommerce flows)

AI-powered static ad creation at volume (portfolio required)

Data-driven, self-directed, comfortable building from scratch

Nice-to-Have:

Klaviyo or email marketing experience

Meta Ads, Google Ads, or TikTok Ads manager

DTC CRO, A/B testing tools (VWO, Optimizely)

HTML/CSS, skincare/beauty category experience

Working Arrangement

1-month paid trial full-time, with growth into DTC Growth Lead

Fully remote, a sync-first, 4 hours/week CT overlap for syncs

We cover all AI tools, Shopify apps, and software — you choose the stack

Direct founder access, full autonomy over workflow

To Apply:

1. Claude CLI demo (mandatory) — Loom video showing you building something with Claude CLI

2. Marketing portfolio — landing pages, static ads, email campaigns, Shopify work. Specialist in one area? Show depth, not breadth

3. Pick any Livaclean product — mock up 1 static ad concept for 3 awareness levels (problem/solution/product-aware)

raw.description:
Job Title

Director, Transaction Management

Job Description Summary

As the Transaction Management Director, you will lead transaction management strategy and execution for large, complex client portfolios and enterprise real estate initiatives across multiple asset classes. This role translates client business objectives into market optimization strategies, transaction plans, portfolio opportunities, and high-quality execution outcomes while leading brokerage resources, transaction teams, and cross-functional partners.

As a member of Cushman & Wakefield’s Portfolio Advisory Group, the Transaction Management Director will be dedicated to one or more of Cushman & Wakefield’s most dynamic client accounts. In this role, you will collaborate closely with peers and the account team to support a client's strategic real estate vision. The Transaction Management Director will embody our team philosophy “Client First, Insight Always, Execution Excellence”, ensuring every deliverable reflects the team’s commitment to innovation, collaboration, and measurable impact.

Job Description

Strategic Portfolio & Market Optimization

  • Lead market optimization planning and strategic transaction initiatives that align with client business goals, portfolio objectives, and real estate priorities.

  • Lead development of strategic real estate plans and provide strategic real estate advice to clients.

  • Identify occupancy cost savings strategies, pull-forward opportunities, expansion and contraction strategies, and other portfolio optimization opportunities.

  • Produce and support business case development, reporting, data analysis, and financial analysis required to complete strategic plans.

Complex Transaction Leadership & Execution

  • Initiate new transactions, dispositions, and renewals, and guide transaction delivery through execution.

  • Manage internal and third-party brokerage resources through the course of transactions, providing strategic direction to brokers and client stakeholders.

  • Lead and oversee aggressive negotiations to deliver favorable outcomes on behalf of the client and support consistent transaction management practices.

  • Execute complex, large transactions with high-level transaction knowledge and oversee legal review of client leased documents.

  • Engage project managers, facility managers, environmental consultants, and other partners as needed to support transaction execution.

Client Relationship & Transaction Governance

  • Partner with client corporate real estate teams and local business unit leaders to understand requirements and build transaction strategies that support client needs.

  • Lead and facilitate client presentations, business reviews, key client meetings, and transaction governance discussions.

  • Partner with clients’ senior-level operational groups to identify real estate needs, transaction priorities, and areas of opportunity.

Reporting, Financial Analysis & Value Creation

  • Maintain and monitor process reporting to clients using a variety of tools and ensure accurate transaction data using various systems.

  • Perform market and financial analysis to support transaction strategy, portfolio recommendations, and client decision making.

  • Manage revenue projections and tracking to support account-level visibility and performance management

  • .

  • Prepare close-out reports and value-add calculations for transactions.

Process Governance, Technology & AI Enablement

  • Coordinate reporting requirements and provide guidance to field agents, service partners, and clients to maximize reporting effectiveness.

  • Modify and adapt process documents and playbooks to meet client requirements.

  • Identify and implement process improvements, innovations, post-transaction reviews, and client survey practices that support continuous improvement.

  • Leverage AI-enabled and technology-driven solutions to improve transaction execution, reporting quality, analysis, workflow efficiency, and client outcomes.

People Leadership & Team Development

  • Manage direct reports through coaching and mentoring to support an engaged, high-performing transaction management team.

  • Lead transaction teams, brokers, field agents, service partners, and cross-functional contributors through complex transaction activity.

  • Maintain a cohesive, performance-measured team environment that supports client satisfaction, work quality, and consistent delivery.




Cushman & Wakefield also provides eligible employees with an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs, generally including health, vision, and dental insurance, flexible spending accounts, health savings accounts, retirement savings plans, life, and disability insurance programs, and paid and unpaid time away from work. In addition to a comprehensive benefits package, Cushman and Wakefield provide eligible employees with competitive pay, which may vary depending on eligibility factors such as geographic location, date of hire, total hours worked, job type, business line, and applicability of collective bargaining agreements.
The compensation that will be offered to the successful candidate will depend on factors such as whether the position is covered by a collective bargaining agreement, the geographic area in which the work will be performed, market pay rates in that area, and the candidate’s experience and qualifications.
The company will not pay less than minimum wage for this role.
The compensation for the position is: $ 148,750.00 - $175,000.00Cushman & Wakefield is an Equal Opportunity employer to all protected groups, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. Discrimination of any type will not be tolerated.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act Amendments Act (ADAAA), if you have a disability and would like to request an accommodation in order to apply for a position at Cushman & Wakefield, please call the ADA line at 1-888-365-5406 or email . Please refer to the job title and job location when you contact us.

Become a part of our caring community

A lead product manager manages multiple simultaneous projects and oversees all aspects of each project, from conception to completion.
Lead product managers may also task themselves with developing new products or features within existing offerings. This requires them to work with other departments —such as engineering, service, ops, sales, etc.—to ensure that they're building something that meets the needs of both the customer and the business.

Key Responsibilities

Product Strategy & Roadmap

  • Lead the product vision and roadmap for assigned digital experiences.
  • Translate our priorities, customer insights, and operational needs into measurable outcomes.
  • Balance near-term delivery with long-term platform evolution.
  • Lead product discovery and identify opportunities that improve customer and outcomes.

Mobile & Digital Experience Leadership

  • Lead strategy and execution of mobile-first customer experiences.
  • Champion intuitive digital journeys across authentication, onboarding, refill, fulfillment, and self-service.
  • Partner with UX and Engineering to improve usability, accessibility, and customer satisfaction.
  • Use customer insights and analytics to prioritize investments.

Capability Thinking & Platform Evolution

  • Identify opportunities to convert channel-specific functionality into reusable platform capabilities.
  • Partner with capability product managers to reduce duplication and increase consistency across channels.
  • Advocate for configurable, scalable solutions over one-off customizations.
  • Help shape our transition toward capability-based product ownership.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Lead teams through discovery, prioritization, delivery, and continuous improvement.
  • Build partnerships across Design, Engineering, Operations, Analytics, and Business teams.

Product Operations & Delivery

  • Lead teams without direct authority.
  • Experience using customer insights and analytics to drive product decisions.
  • Experience identifying reusable solutions and influence platform strategy.
  • Experience working within Agile product organizations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Healthcare, pharmacy, or other regulated industry experience.

  • Experience partnering with platform engineering teams.

This role is responsible for generating weekly and monthly performance reports, tracking service-level agreements (SLAs), analyzing alert trends, and identifying areas for system and operational improvement.

The Data Analyst supports the PMO, dashboard teams, engineering teams, and operations staff by transforming raw operational data into clear, actionable insights. This includes KPI development, trend identification, and metric reconciliation to ensure reporting accuracy across the enterprise.

This position is fully remote.

  • Develop KPI calculations and performance measurement frameworks.

  • Experience producing weekly/monthly reports for federal, DoD, or large enterprise environments.
  • Experience analyzing alert logs, incidents, or operational performance datasets.

Technical Knowledge (Required)

  • Proficiency with Excel, SQL, or analytical tools for data querying and reporting.
  • Understanding of KPI design, SLA metrics, and performance measurement methodologies.
  • Familiarity with dashboards or BI tools like Power BI, Tableau, or Grafana.

Required:

Skills

NRG is seeking a Director to join its Growth & Partnerships organization. This role is ideal for an analytically rigorous energy leader who excels at creating structure, aligning cross-functional teams, and establishing repeatable processes that improve how complex opportunities are evaluated and advanced.

The Director will build the internal programs, decision systems, governance, and analytical standards that enable the Growth & Partnerships organization to execute consistently and at a high level. This leader will create the structure, cross-functional alignment, and operating discipline needed to translate complex growth opportunities into clear priorities, rigorous analysis, and executable plans.

Working across internal functions, the Director will create consistency across opportunity portfolios, and ensure leaders receive comparable, decision-ready analysis. The role will partner closely with NRG’s operating businesses and Finance, Regulatory, Legal, Operations, Technology, Development, and other functions to move priority opportunities through a clear, disciplined path from initial thesis to validation, investment decision, and transition to scale.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and manage a common operating system for the Growth & Partnerships organization, including opportunity intake, prioritization, workplans, stage gates, decision rights, governance forums, and transition criteria.

  • Create and drive decision-making systems that help leadership allocate resources, resolve tradeoffs, and advance the highest-value opportunities with discipline.

  • Establish a consistent analytical framework for evaluating opportunities across markets, business units, technologies, and time horizons.

  • Set and uphold a high bar for business cases, financial models, market assessments, customer value propositions, risk analysis, and executive recommendations; ensure assumptions and logic are transparent and defensible.

  • Integrate opportunity portfolios into a coherent enterprise pipeline, enabling teams to focus on developing opportunities while maintaining consistent priorities, processes, and execution standards across the organization.

  • Lead cross-functional growth programs that bring together commercial, Finance, Regulatory, Legal, Operations, Technology, Development, Strategy, and business-unit teams around shared outcomes.

  • Build trusted internal relationships, clarify roles and accountabilities, surface dependencies, and create practical pathways through organizational complexity.

  • Develop reusable tools, templates, data standards, and reporting mechanisms that improve the quality, consistency, and speed of work across the organization.

  • Maintain enterprise visibility into portfolio status, resource needs, risks, open questions, milestones, and upcoming decisions.

  • Translate complex cross-functional work into clear, executive-ready materials and integrated recommendations for senior leadership and Board discussions.

  • Support pilot governance and transition planning so validated opportunities move cleanly to the business units best positioned to scale them.

What We Are Looking For

  • Enterprise operators who know how to build the programs, processes, and operating rhythms that make a new organization effective.

  • Patient bridge-builders who can establish trust, navigate internally, and align stakeholders with different goals, constraints, and perspectives.

  • Structured problem solvers who turn ambiguity into practical workplans, decision frameworks, governance, and clear accountability.

  • Analytically rigorous leaders who remain close enough to the work to test the logic, challenge assumptions, and raise the quality of models and recommendations.

  • Cross-functional leaders who create momentum through influence, follow-through, and disciplined coordination rather than formal authority.

  • Systems thinkers who can identify common requirements across distinct opportunity portfolios while preserving appropriate flexibility.

  • Strong communicators who translate complex technical, regulatory, operational, and financial issues into clear choices for senior stakeholders.

  • Collaborative peers who complement externally oriented growth leaders and take pride in enabling the entire team to perform at a consistently high level.

  • Leaders who demonstrate sound judgment, intellectual honesty, ownership, persistence, and a commitment to measurable outcomes.

Preferred Experience

  • 10–15+ years of experience in enterprise strategy, program leadership, strategic finance, management consulting, operations, business transformation, market development, or a related field.

  • Demonstrated experience creating and implementing decision systems, governance models, stage gates, portfolio processes, or other operating mechanisms for complex cross-functional work.

  • Recent hands-on experience building or reviewing sophisticated financial models and analytical frameworks, with the ability to understand the underlying logic rather than simply replicate an existing analysis.

  • Significant experience in energy, utilities, competitive power markets, distributed energy resources, demand response, energy technology, infrastructure, data centers, industrial energy management, or a closely related sector.

  • Technical knowledge of energy markets, including regulated ecosystems, and the ability to quickly understand complex commercial, regulatory, operational, and financial environments.

  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and influencing senior stakeholders without relying on direct authority.

  • Experience standardizing methods, data, assumptions, reporting, or decision criteria across teams or business units.

  • Familiarity with one or more of the following areas: wholesale power and generation economics; retail energy and customer solutions; data center and hyperscaler energy needs; utility partnerships and regulation; DERs, demand response, load flexibility, or virtual power plants; corporate development, investment analysis, or commercialization of new products and services.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Energy Systems, Public Policy, or a related discipline.

  • MBA, master’s degree, or other advanced degree preferred but not required.

Success in This Role

  • Establish a trusted, repeatable operating system that gives Growth & Partnerships a shared language, cadence, and path from opportunity intake through decision and transition.

  • Create consistent analytical and decision standards across opportunity portfolios and supporting teams.

  • Enable teams to develop clear, comparable business cases, financial models, assumptions, and executive recommendations that support effective enterprise decision-making.

  • Build strong internal partnerships and make cross-functional engagement more efficient, transparent, and accountable.

  • Give leadership timely visibility into portfolio progress, tradeoffs, resource needs, risks, and required decisions.

  • Enable opportunity teams to move faster without sacrificing rigor, collaboration, or effective governance.

  • Develop a reputation as the internal integrator who helps Growth & Partnerships operate as one coordinated enterprise platform.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Patient Coordinator plays a critical inside sales role in driving the success of Natera’s Oncology product lines. This position is responsible for managing and growing patient relationships while directly contributing to revenue through proactive outreach, pipeline development, and ongoing engagement.

As a primary point of contact for patients, the Patient Coordinator partners closely with Field Sales, Operations, and internal stakeholders to execute territory strategies, advance opportunities through the sales pipeline, and ensure timely testing and repeat utilization. This role blends customer advocacy with inside sales execution, requiring strong relationship-building skills, sales acumen, and the ability to connect daily activities to pipeline and revenue outcomes.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Serve as an inside sales partner to Field Sales by supporting territory strategies and advancing opportunities through the pipeline.
  • Proactively manage inbound and outbound patient outreach to influence testing adoption, scheduling, and continuity of care.
  • Build and maintain long-term, consultative relationships with patients to drive repeat testing and ongoing engagement.
  • Identify, nurture, and progress patient opportunities from initial contact through completion of testing, ensuring alignment with sales pipeline goals.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Billing and Customer Support to remove barriers and close gaps impacting conversion or timing.
  • Assess patient needs with a solutions-oriented mindset, addressing logistical, clinical coordination, and service challenges.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of interactions, opportunities, and pipeline activity in CRM and business intelligence tools (e.g., Salesforce, PowerBI).
  • Analyze territory and pipeline data to prioritize outreach, identify trends, and optimize sales efforts.
  • Ensure timely completion of data requests and reporting related to sales performance and patient engagement.
  • Act as a patient advocate within Natera while maintaining a revenue-focused, sales-driven approach.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Compliance & Training

  • Regularly works with PHI in both paper and electronic formats.
  • Completes HIPAA/PHI privacy, security, and General Policies and Procedures training within required timelines.
  • Maintains current status on all Natera-required training.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum of 2 years of inside sales experience, preferably in a remote or phone-based environment.
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in outbound and inbound sales or call center roles with measurable performance goals.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage a territory or book of business and connect daily activities to pipeline outcomes.
  • Experience using CRM systems (Salesforce preferred) to manage leads, opportunities, and sales activity.
  • Background in medical, diagnostic, or biological sciences preferred

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Strong relationship-building skills with the ability to influence and guide patients through a consultative sales process.
  • Proven ability to execute inside sales strategies while thinking strategically about territory and pipeline management.
  • Comfortable handling objections, navigating complex conversations, and driving next steps toward conversion.
  • Results-oriented mindset with a strong sense of urgency and accountability.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with strong presentation ability.
  • Ability to analyze data and pipeline metrics to prioritize outreach and optimize performance.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Google platform and business reporting tools.
  • Self-motivated, adaptable, and effective working independently in a fast-paced, remote or hybrid environment.
  • Team-first attitude with a strong collaborative approach across sales and operational partners.
The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations.

$77,200—$85,000 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

Defined responsibilities, authorities and accountabilities

  • Define and maintain the global business development roadmap for all Medical schemes, aligned with the Medical Devices strategy and growth priorities.
  • Lead the Global Medical Business Development strategy and coordinate business development initiatives across countries, DOs and Hubs.
  • Build a structured view of market trends, client needs, competitor activity, regulatory developments and pricing dynamics to identify and prioritise growth opportunities.
  • Develop business cases and coordinate the incubation, launch and scaling of new or enhanced Medical certification schemes and service offerings.

  • Facilitate transparent sharing of qualified opportunities and market intelligence across the network and promote consistent use of relevant CRM and reporting platforms.

Areas of accountability as member of the Global Leadership Team

  • Drive standardisation and harmonisation of processes across schemes and regions – within areas of responsibilities.

  • Strong facilitation, communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement capabilities across commercial, technical, regulatory and operational functions.
  • Demonstrated ability to work proactively and independently, taking ownership of global initiatives from concept through implementation.
  • Strong organisational, project and change management capabilities.
  • Strong commercial acumen and deep appreciation of the TIC industry.
  • Familiarity with conformity assessment procedures and Notified Body operations.
  • Multilingual proficiency and cross-cultural experience.

Essential

raw.description:
Engineering Lead

Large, Complex Federal Government Program | Full-Time W-2 | Fully Remote (U.S.)

The Problem We're Hiring You to Solve

Monthly production releases. Zero escaped critical defects. Most engineering organizations treat those as a tradeoff. On this program they are both commitments, measured every release, in front of the customer.

We are hiring the engineering leader who builds an organization that delivers both at once: multiple cross-functional development teams modernizing a federal home loan benefit platform while sustaining the 20-year-old system it replaces. If you believe speed and quality are the same discipline practiced well, and you have the delivery record to prove it, keep reading.

The Opportunity

Most engineering leadership roles ask you to protect a delivery machine someone else built. This one asks you to build the machine.

The program spans multiple development teams working in parallel across a modern platform (Salesforce-centered, configuration-first, supplemented by serverless capabilities in a government cloud) and a legacy suite that must stay stable until it is decommissioned. Work arrives through a formal intake process that turns business needs into executable plans with committed scope, timelines, and team sizing in days. Then your organization delivers against those commitments, publicly and measurably.

The quality bar is unusually explicit. Every release ships with 100% automated test coverage for its features before user acceptance testing begins. Defect detection before UAT must exceed 95%. Escaped critical defects must be zero. Critical production bugs get fixed in three days. Accessibility and security compliance are release gates, not aspirations. These are not stretch goals on a slide. They are how the program measures the engineering organization every month.

That bar is exactly why this role is interesting. Hitting it once takes heroics. Hitting it every month takes an engineering system: disciplined definition of done, test automation as a first-class craft, engineers who own quality instead of throwing code over a wall, and a leader who builds all of that into how teams work rather than inspecting it in afterward. That leader is you.

You will work alongside a Senior DevSecOps & Platform Engineering Lead who owns the delivery pipeline and an Enterprise Solution Architect who owns the designs. You own the organization that turns those designs into shipped, tested, production software.

What You'll Own

  • The engineering organization. Lead multiple cross-functional development teams across modern and legacy platforms, flexing team size and composition as workflows through intake. Teams form, deliver, and re-form around the work. You make that fluid instead of chaotic.
  • Delivery you put your name on. Commit to scope, level of effort, and timelines in executable plans, then hit them. When you cannot, say so early, with a recovery plan, before the customer discovers it.
  • A quality system, not a QA gate. Engineer quality into how teams work: definition of done that includes full automated testing, code review that catches problems, and metrics that surface risk early. The outcomes that prove it: zero escaped critical defects, defect detection above 95% before UAT, and critical fixes inside three days.
  • Test automation as a craft. Build the discipline where every feature ships with complete positive and negative automated coverage, and the regression suite becomes the safety net the customer trusts enough to focus UAT on new functionality only.
  • The monthly release drumbeat. Production value ships every 30 days or faster, release after release, without burning the team down to do it.
  • Dual-stack engineering. Run modern configuration-first platform development and legacy sustainment side by side, including the warranty on everything your teams release.
  • Engineering standards that outlast you. Set and enforce the bar for code quality, review, documentation, and definition of done across every team, and keep documentation current with every release because the program requires it and good engineering does too.
  • AI-native development at team scale. Make AI-assisted engineering the norm across your organization, not the hobby of your three most curious engineers, while holding AI-assisted work to the same zero-escaped-defect bar as everything else.
  • The talent engine. Hire deliberately, grow engineers visibly, retain the strong ones, and raise the bar with every addition.

AI-Native Engineering at Team Scale

AI is part of how PhoenixTeam works. Plenty of leaders can use AI tools themselves. This role is about something harder: making an entire engineering organization genuinely better with them.

We are looking for someone who already uses tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot in their own work, and who has begun leading teams through the shift: establishing standards for responsible AI-assisted development, using AI to expand automated test coverage and accelerate code review, applying it to defect analysis and documentation, and measuring whether it actually improved throughput and quality rather than assuming it did.

The accountability question matters most in a federal environment with a zero-escaped-critical-defect standard. AI-generated code is your teams' code. It gets the same review, the same testing, and the same ownership as anything an engineer typed by hand. You set that culture.

Boundaries are non-negotiable: federal environments govern what tools may touch government code, systems, and data. Use AI wherever it creates leverage, and understand the security, data, privacy, and authorization boundaries governing where and how it can be used.

Tools will change. The leadership behavior we are hiring for will not: continually ask where your organization's engineering hours are going and eliminate the waste responsibly.

What Great Looks Like

Twelve months in, we would expect to see:

  1. The cadence held. Production value shipped at least monthly, every month, with zero escaped critical defects and a team that is energized rather than exhausted.
  2. The regression suite earned trust. Automated coverage is complete enough that UAT focuses on new features, and the customer stopped asking whether old functionality still works.
  3. Quality metrics are boring in the best way. Detection rates above 95%, critical fixes inside three days, and defect trends the customer reviews without concern.
  4. Teams flex without drama. Work moves from intake to a staffed, productive team quickly, and re-forming teams around new work stopped being disruptive.
  5. AI lifted the organization measurably. Throughput and coverage improved with AI-assisted engineering, defect rates did not, and your standards for responsible use became the program's standards.
  6. Both stacks are healthy. Legacy sustainment is quiet and predictable while modern platform velocity grows quarter over quarter.
  7. The bench is stronger. Engineers you hired and grew are visibly better, your leads lead, and departures are rare and regretted.
  8. The customer asks for more. Delivery confidence earned the program expanded scope.

What You Bring

We care about evidence more than resumes. Expect us to ask what your organizations shipped, what your defect and delivery metrics actually were, how you turned around a team that was missing its commitments, and how AI functions across your teams today.

  • A multi-team delivery record. You have led engineering organizations of multiple teams building and shipping production software, and you can walk us through the delivery and quality outcomes with numbers.
  • Hands-on credibility. You still read code, review designs, and go deep when it matters. Engineers respect your technical judgment, not just your title.
  • A quality system you built. You have taken an organization to measurably low defect escape rates through engineering discipline and test automation, not through more manual QA at the end.
  • Federal delivery experience. You have shipped software inside a regulated federal environment and treat security, accessibility, authorization, and documentation requirements as delivery constraints to engineer within, not excuses for slipping.
  • Metrics fluency. You run engineering organizations on evidence: release cadence, defect detection and escape rates, cycle times, automation coverage, and you use those numbers to improve the system rather than to punish people.
  • AI-forward leadership. You use AI engineering tools yourself and have led teams into using them well, with standards, measurement, and accountability.
  • Customer-facing composure. You present delivery status, defend engineering decisions with evidence, deliver bad news early, and challenge unrealistic direction respectfully, including ours.
  • Talent judgment. You hire well, grow engineers deliberately, and make hard calls about performance without outsourcing them to HR processes.

  • U.S.-based, and able to obtain and maintain a federal Public Trust clearance.

We do not screen on degrees or year counts. If your evidence is strong, we want to talk.

Helpful, Not Required

  • Salesforce delivery leadership, or leadership of teams on a comparable configuration-first enterprise platform.
  • Deep background in test automation frameworks and strategy.
  • Experience running legacy sustainment and modernization in parallel, or decommissioning a production system.
  • Familiarity with 508 accessibility compliance in delivery.
  • Mortgage or housing finance experience is not required. We will teach you the domain.

Leadership Expectations

This is an organizational leadership role with a hands-on soul.

You own outcomes across multiple teams, which means your leverage comes through leads, standards, and systems rather than personal output. But you stay close enough to the work to know when a design is wrong, an estimate is padded, or a team is quietly drowning. Engineers should experience you as a leader who understands what they do, because you can still do it.

You work directly with federal customers and decision-makers. You present delivery status with candor, defend your teams' engineering decisions with evidence, and challenge poor technical or program direction respectfully. Silent disagreement is a failure mode here, and so is shielding the customer from bad news until it becomes a crisis.

You develop the leaders under you deliberately, and you hold the engineering bar even when the schedule argues against it, because on this program the quality metrics are the schedule.

You'll Probably Love This Role If...

You are the leader whose teams ship on a rhythm others find implausible, and you can explain exactly which disciplines make it possible. You think a public, measured quality bar is a gift, because it settles arguments that consume other organizations. You would rather build a delivery machine than inherit one. You like customers in the room. And you are genuinely energized by leading engineers through the AI shift, because you have seen what it does for a team that adopts it seriously.

This May Not Be the Role for You If...

We would rather you self-select now than be unhappy in month three. You may struggle here if you:

  • Lead from dashboards and status meetings, and stopped engaging with the actual engineering.
  • Treat quality as the QA team's job rather than an engineering outcome you own.
  • Negotiate quality bars down when schedules get tight.
  • Hide delivery risk from customers until it becomes undeniable.
  • Prefer stable, fixed teams and find flexing around the work disruptive.
  • View AI as a novelty rather than an engineering capability your organization must master.
  • Stopped learning when you became senior.

None of that makes someone a bad leader. It makes them a bad fit for this particular job.

Why PhoenixTeam

  • We are practitioners, not a staffing shop. PhoenixTeam is a woman-owned small business founded and led by housing finance technologists who still do the work. Our teams have spent years embedded inside federal housing programs, from loan guaranty to rural housing lending to mortgage insurance. You will build your organization alongside leaders who have shipped, not above account managers who have not.
  • Your leadership has visible consequences. Delivery cadence, quality, and reliability are measured monthly and reviewed by the customer. The organization you build performs in public.
  • Direct customer access. You work with federal decision-makers yourself. Your judgment reaches the people who act on it, without three layers of translation in between.
  • You build the machine. You are establishing how engineering delivery works on this program, not maintaining someone else's operating model.
  • AI-native is practice, not positioning. AI is part of how PhoenixTeam delivers, and we fund ongoing AI education and development for the entire team. In this role you will scale that investment across an organization, not fight for permission to use it.
  • Fully remote,S.-based, permanently.
  • Competitive salary and 100% employer-paid medical insurance.
  • Mission you can explain at dinner. The software your teams ship supports a home loan benefit for the people who served this country.

Position Requirements

  • Full-time W-2 employment with PhoenixTeam.
  • Must be based in the United States.
  • Fully remote.
  • Work supports a federal civilian agency.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain the required federal Public Trust clearance. A Secret clearance is not required.

PhoenixTeam is a woman-owned small business focused on federal and commercial housing finance technology.

Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed above are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and are not necessarily all-inclusive.

raw.description:
Responsibilities

Peraton's Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

Peraton is seeking a Senior Cloud Data Architect SME with expertise in Databricks and cloud data lakehouse architectures to lead the data engineering foundation for a federal data migration program. You will design and oversee the implementation of ETL pipelines, schema harmonization, and data quality frameworks within a FedRAMP-compliant hybrid AWS cloud environment.

Work Location: Remote

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Lead the design and implementation of the cloud data lakehouse architecture for federal species data ingestion, ensuring compatibility with existing infrastructure and platform constraints
  • Design the Delta Live Tables ETL pipeline architecture, defining pipeline topology, data flow patterns, transformation stages, and error-handling frameworks
  • Lead schema harmonization activities, conducting gap analysis between source schemas and the target data model and producing field-level mapping documentation
  • Define metadata standards for all ingested datasets including naming conventions, data types, null handling, and authoritative source attribution
  • Design the Metadata and Authoritative Source Registry structure and population methodology
  • Oversee ETL pipeline development and deployment, ensuring all pipelines are version-controlled and peer-reviewed
  • Design data quality validation frameworks within ETL pipelines, defining completeness, accuracy, consistency, and spatial integrity quality criteria
  • Produce the Data Model Harmonization Report, documenting gap analysis findings between source schemas and the target data model, field-level mapping decisions, and metadata standard definitions for government review and approval
  • Lead the operational handoff of ETL pipeline architecture, producing documentation for routine data refresh, pipeline monitoring, and maintenance procedures
  • Provide cloud data architecture guidance for FedRAMP-compliant production deployment

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelors degree and 12 years professional experience or a Masters degree and 10 years professional experience or an Associates degree and 14 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 16 years’ professional experience.
  • U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance
  • Extensive years of experience in cloud data architecture with expertise in Databricks and Delta Lake/Delta Live Tables
  • Demonstrated experience designing data lakehouse architectures for large-scale data migration programs
  • Experience with schema harmonization, ETL pipeline design, and data quality frameworks
  • Strong knowledge of FedRAMP, FISMA, and federal cloud compliance requirements
  • Experience with metadata management and authoritative source registry design

Preferred Qualifications

  • Databricks Certified Data Engineer or equivalent certification
  • AWS Certified Solutions Architect or AWS Certified Data Engineer certification
  • Experience with federal environmental or geospatial data systems
  • Familiarity with spatial data integration and GIS data pipelines
  • Active Public Trust Clearance

Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Target Salary Range

$135,000 - $216,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

EEO

At TeamFicient, our team spans multiple countries and regions, and we stay connected by operating within EST, CST, and PST time zones.

TeamFicient is looking for an experienced AI Developer/Engineer to design, build, and scale production-grade AI applications that deliver real value to our clients. You'll work at the intersection of applied AI, backend engineering, and cloud infrastructure, building systems that are robust, reliable, and ready for the real world. If you have a proven track record of shipping LLM and RAG-based systems in production, this role is for you.

AI Application Development

Cloud and Infrastructure

Good to Haves

raw.description:
Are you looking for limitless career opportunities with a company that values growth, innovation, and teamwork? At Ntiva, we’re more than a Managed Services Provider, we’re a community dedicated to helping each other, our clients, and their businesses thrive both personally and professionally. Ntiva is a culture of people who are passionate about the work…and each other.

Our clients view us as an essential part of their teams, relying on us for strategic guidance, fast solutions to complex challenges, and proactive support. With strategic locations across the U.S. and leadership from our founder, Steven Freidkin, we’re on the front lines of a fast-paced industry, facing cybersecurity threats and rapid technology changes together.

If you thrive in a dynamic, supportive environment and enjoy going above and beyond, we’d love to meet you. Come explore one of our many opportunities and grow with us!

How you’ll make an Impact

As a Service Desk Technician II within the Dental Division, you'll be a vital member of our team providing top-tier support to clients. This client-facing role involves regular interaction via phone, email, and remote assistance tools, requiring excellent communication skills and a focus on delivering outstanding client service.
Your primary responsibilities include resolving workstation, server, and network-related tickets, managing advanced systems troubleshooting, and completing assigned project tasks. You will escalate issues to the Director of Operations when necessary, ensuring that more complex challenges are handled swiftly and efficiently. You will also act as a key escalation point for Level 3 team leads, helping to manage client expectations and ensuring seamless support during the escalation process.
This position requires the application of a wide range of specialized skills, frequently adapting tools, procedures, and techniques to meet the unique needs of our clients. As an escalation engineer, your role demands originality and ingenuity in establishing new procedures within functional areas. Your experience and sound judgment will be essential in planning and executing assigned tasks.

Location and Work Expectations

  • This is a remote position; however, team members should be willing and able to travel if the need arises, though such travel is expected to be infrequent. Candidates with proximity to one of our Centers of Excellence are preferred (Lombard, IL; McLean, VA; Shreveport, LA; Overland Park, KS).
  • Monday-Friday, 10am-7pm CST
  • This role also includes participation in a rotating on-call schedule.

What you will be doing

  • Maintain a strong focus on providing excellent customer service
  • Provide responsive client service via phone, email, and in person interactions
  • Answer internal and external client/vendor calls quickly and pleasantly
  • Communicate in a friendly, professional and patient manner
  • Perform all duties with the goal of building and maintaining long-term client/vendor relationships
  • Maintain exceptional client service, understanding client satisfaction and perception is key to a successful relationship with clients
  • IT support services for clients’ infrastructure, including clients’ core business applications
  • Acquire specific knowledge of the client and how IT relates to their business
  • Develop in-depth knowledge of the service offerings and how they relate to clients’ needs
  • Participate in projects by performing assigned duties
  • Perform other related technical duties as assigned
  • Identify clients’ needs and report to Director of Operations/Team Lead
  • Update documentation for client configurations or processes
  • Communicate managed services installation and maintenance with Centralized Services (CS)
  • Communicate with the client regularly to keep informed of technical support progress and notify of impending changes or expected outages
  • Utilize active listening and client-care skills in identifying potential concerns
  • Report client concerns or complaints to Director of Operations & Team
  • Lead, and manage urgent requests and escalations with patience and empathy
  • Answer internal and external communications timely and professionally
  • Contact client within 2 business days for tickets in Follow Up status unless issue requires further delay as notated on the ticket
  • Close tickets within 5 business days unless issue requires further delay as notated on the ticket

You'll be successful in this role if you have

  • A minimum of 4 years of recent Dental-related IT experience in a Technical Support environment
  • Dental Hardware Experience:
    • Intraoral Cameras
    • Intraoral Sensors
    • Intraoral Scanners
    • Extraoral Sensors (CBCT / Pano / Ceph)
    • Vitals Monitors
  • Proven experience with Windows workstation repair, maintenance, diagnosing and troubleshooting hardware and operating system related issues
  • Strong documentation skills, including documentation of security incidents, end user training and new hardware deployment
  • Proficiency in configuring & troubleshooting network settings on workstations and network devices such as modems, firewalls, and managed switches
  • Proficiency in Hypervisor & virtual desktop client support
  • Proficiency in Office 365 account and client support
  • Proficiency with Exchange mailbox administration
  • Proficiency with Server backup monitoring and maintenance
  • Proficiency in wireless connectivity for mobile devices and workstations
  • Proficiency with Mobile device support – smartphones, tablets and laptops
  • Proficiency with Active Directory account creation and management
  • Proficiency with Network drive and printer mappings
  • Ability to diagnose network connectivity issues for workstations and servers
  • Ability to communicate and work effectively with end users over the phone and on-site
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with ability to translate or quickly learn to translate technical terms to business language for non-technical clients
  • Exemplify professionalism and business etiquette in all communication, including in-person, email, and phone interactions with client end users and colleagues
  • Critical thinking and problem-solving skills
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Past experience and desire to work as a part of a team
  • This role involves extended periods of sitting or standing and regular use of computers and office equipment

Required language skills

  • Ability to communicate professionally, in English, both written and orally
  • Ability to write business correspondence and process procedures
  • Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, and the general public

Bonus points for

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred in IT, IS, CS, or another technical discipline
  • CompTIA certifications preferred
  • Microsoft Technology Associate (MTA) preferred
  • Fortinet Certification (preferred, required if offered a position)
  • 2 years of recent leadership positions or relevant experience

Benefits and Perks

  • Medical, Dental and Vision coverage for employee and family
  • 401k + company-matched contributions 4% match on 5% contribution - no vesting period! (Employee and Company contribute after 90 days)
  • Group Term Life and Accidental Death and Dismemberment coverage (company provided)
  • Short-Term (voluntary enrollment) and Long-Term Disability coverage (company provided)
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) Options / PPO Options
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Paid Time Off (PTO) + Volunteer Time Off (VTO) + 8 Paid Holidays + 3 Floating Holidays
  • Education Reimbursement Program
  • Generous Employee Referral Program - cash bonus for successful referrals!
  • Dynamic Recognition and Rewards
  • Clear Promotion and Advancement Tracks
  • Work with Industry-Leading Talent

The base pay range for this position is expected to be between $49,000.00 and $70,000.00 per year. The base pay offered may vary depending on multiple non-discriminatory factors including, but not limited to, market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position also includes medical benefits, 401(k) eligibility, and PTO. Additional details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.

FLSA Status: Salaried, Non-Exempt

Work Authorization Criteria
We welcome applicants who are U.S. persons. At this time, we are unable to offer sponsorship or assume sponsorship of an employment visa.

Workspace Requirements and Remote Work Policy
Team members must establish a dedicated safe workspace that is free from distractions, hazards, and that is secure from unauthorized access. This includes following Ntiva’s IT User and Security Policies that include but are not limited to password-protecting all equipment, keeping confidential and proprietary documents secure, refraining from using public Wi-Fi, having adequate arrangements in place to avoid significant interruptions from caregiving responsibilities during work hours (except in emergency situations with manager approval). Any remote work away from a team member’s normal expected dedicated safe workspace must be requested by team member, is subject to review by management, and must adhere to Ntiva policies and procedures.

Our Commitment to a Diverse Workforce
At Ntiva, we are committed to creating and maintaining a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming work environment for all employees and job applicants. We firmly believe that a diverse workforce fosters a wider range of perspectives, experiences, and ideas that lead to increased creativity, innovation, and problem-solving capabilities. raw.description:
About Outreach

Outreach, founded in 2014, is the only complete agentic AI platform for revenue teams. Outreach infuses agentic AI, conversation intelligence, and assistive AI to power hundreds of use cases across revenue motions. From new logo prospecting to expansions, deal acceleration, driving retention, and forecasting, Outreach AI automates workflows and frees sellers to focus on more strategic conversations and actions. Revenue leaders benefit from connected account visibility, performance insights, and higher forecasting accuracy across every GTM team. World leading enterprise organizations use Outreach to power their revenue teams, including Databricks, SAP, Siemens, and Verizon to name a few.

About the Team

Our Senior Account Executive, Enterprise team partners with prospective customers of 5,000 to 10,000 employees, owning the full deal cycle from first conversation to signed contract. We are product experts and ambassadors for Outreach, building deep knowledge of our customers' goals and pain points so they can create and close pipeline through the Outreach Sales Execution Platform.

We enjoy learning new sales trends and methodologies, going to industry events, subscribing to blogs and podcasts, reading books, and researching case studies so we can grow together. We work closely to champion our customers, share success stories, and celebrate our wins.

The Role

The primary purpose of a Senior Account Executive, Enterprise at Outreach is to lead complex, full-lifecycle sales strategy for net new, prospect accounts. This is a pure hunter role.Hunters at Outreach own the entire sales cycle, including researching, prospecting, advising, negotiating contracts, and closing deals. You are accountable for developing account plans, using the MEDDPICC sales methodology to build new business and achieve your territory goals. You identify and deeply understand a prospect's needs, pains, and desired business outcomes, then build an effective business case that demonstrates the ROI and value of the Outreach platform. You will partner with other members of the go-to-market team, such as Solutions Consultants, to guide prospective customers through proof of concept demos. Your primary points of contact are executive stakeholders (CRO, COO, CEO, CFO, and CISO). Key performance indicators include quota attainment, pipeline generation and coverage, and forecast quality and accuracy.

We are an AI-forward team, using intelligent tools to research accounts, sharpen discovery, and build business cases faster than the market moves. We are looking for sellers who bring that same mindset to the C-suite, helping prospects see how Outreach's AI-powered platform turns their pipeline into predictable revenue.

Your Daily Adventures Will Include

    • Territory and Pipeline: Identify, research, and qualify potential new customers in your assigned territory, building pipeline coverage sufficient to achieve your sales targets.

    • Forecasting: Forecast deals accurately using Outreach's forecast methodology.

    • Account Planning: Develop and deliver on account plans that strategically increase new revenue for Outreach.

    • Discovery: Conduct effective discovery calls to identify and unlock the business challenges that Outreach solves.

    • Solution Demonstration: Demonstrate how the Outreach platform delivers a tailored solution to the outcomes a prospect is trying to achieve.

    • Deal Execution: Negotiate contracts with cross-functional stakeholders including C-suite, finance, procurement, and technical teams, partnering with internal go-to-market, finance, and leadership resources to drive deals to close.

    • Scoping and Handoff: Define accurate scoping and success criteria to position a successful implementation, and provide a smooth account transition to professional services and account management teams for future adoption and expansion.

Our Vision of You

    • At least 7 years of sales lifecycle management experience, preferably in a SaaS environment

    • Comfortable in a hunting role that is heavily focused on month over month pipeline creation

    • Proven experience selling AI-powered, complex solutions into medium to large organizations

    • Demonstrated curiosity about AI and emerging technologies, with a desire to explore how they can enhance your workflow and drive better outcomes for customers

    • Proven experience selling into accounts through a top-down executive motion

    • Ability to manage and navigate long sales cycles, typically nine to twelve months, with contract values of $200k to $500k

    • Knowledge of the MEDDPICC Sales Methodology and experience applying this framework successfully

    • Disciplined pipeline management, with the rigor to keep opportunities progressing through every stage and forecasts reliable

    • Strong negotiation skills, with the ability to hold value in complex, multi-stakeholder contract discussions

    • Ability to build and cultivate strong, trusting relationships and partnerships, both internally and externally

    • Effective communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to tailor messaging appropriately for the audience

    • Executive presence and interpersonal skills

    • Strong business and financial acumen to be able to showcase metrics and potential ROI

    • High personal integrity, with a commitment to internal processes and sales methodologies

    • A collaborative approach and self-directed drive, with the initiative to keep opportunities moving forward

Why You’ll Love It Here

• Flexible time off
• 401k to help you save for the future
• Generous medical, dental, and vision coverage for full-time employees and their dependents
• A parental leave program that includes options for a paid night nurse, and a gradual return to work
• Infertility/ assisted reproductive services benefit
• Employee referral bonuses to encourage the addition of great new people to the team
• Snacks and beverages in the Office, along with fun events to celebrate
• Diversity and inclusion programs that promote employee resource groups like Outreach Women's Network, Latinx community, Outreach Black Connection, AAPI community, Pride/LGBTQIA+, Gender+, Disability Community, and Veterans/Military
Outreach is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.
Our success is reliant on building teams that include people from different backgrounds and experiences who can elevate assumptions and ideas with fresh perspectives. We're dedicated to hiring the whole human, not just a resume. To that end, we look for a diverse pool of applicants-including those from historically marginalized groups. We would like to invite you to apply even if you don't think you meet all of the requirements listed below. We don't want a few lines in a job description to get between us and the opportunity to meet you.

Working Pattern: Fractional – approximately 6–8 hours per week
Environment: Early-Stage FinTech / People Operations

About the Opportunity

Our client is an early-stage FinTech currently building out its team, leadership capability and internal infrastructure.

As part of this development, the company is looking for a Fractional HR Officer to provide practical People Operations support under the direction of an experienced senior People leader.

This opportunity is particularly suited to an early-career HR professional who already has some practical HR experience but is looking to broaden their exposure, develop their capability and take on increasing responsibility.

You will gain exposure to a wide range of People activity within an early-stage organisation, including recruitment, onboarding, People administration, documentation, employee/consultant records and the development of People processes.

This is not an opportunity for somebody seeking purely observational HR experience. You will be expected to contribute practically, take responsibility for agreed tasks and handle sensitive information appropriately.

In return, there is significant opportunity to learn, develop and gain exposure to the practical development of a People function from an early stage.

Further details regarding the engagement and participation structure will be discussed directly with candidates progressing through the process.

Application – Mandatory Qualifying Questions

Please submit your CV together with a cover letter. Within your cover letter, you must answer each of the mandatory qualifying questions below.

  1. What practical HR or People Operations experience do you currently have? Please describe your responsibilities rather than simply providing your job title.
  2. What CIPD qualification have you completed or are you currently studying? Please state whether this is CIPD Level 3 or Level 5, together with your expected completion date if you are still studying.
  3. What experience do you have supporting employee, worker or contractor onboarding and offboarding?
  4. What experience do you have maintaining confidential People records, HR documentation or personnel files?
  5. What recruitment administration or coordination experience do you have?
  6. Please provide an example of an HR/People process that you have personally administered from beginning to end.
  7. This role involves handling confidential employee, candidate and business information. Please describe your experience handling sensitive information and how you ensure confidentiality and accuracy.
  8. What are you hoping to learn or develop through an opportunity like this?
  9. This opportunity requires approximately 6–8 hours per week. Can you consistently commit to this level of involvement alongside your other professional or study commitments?

These questions are mandatory and form part of our initial assessment process. Applications that do not provide a clear answer to every mandatory qualifying question will be automatically disqualified and will not be considered further in the recruitment process.

What You'll Be Doing

Working under the direction of senior People leadership, you will provide practical support across the developing People function.

Your responsibilities are likely to include:

  • Supporting recruitment administration and coordination
  • Maintaining candidate and recruitment trackers
  • Coordinating interviews and recruitment documentation
  • Supporting onboarding and offboarding processes
  • Maintaining accurate People records
  • Organising employee and consultant documentation
  • Monitoring outstanding documentation and following up where required
  • Supporting contract and People-document administration
  • Maintaining appropriate People trackers and audit trails
  • Drafting routine People correspondence
  • Supporting the organisation and maintenance of People policies and processes
  • Helping maintain accurate records relating to confidentiality and other engagement documentation
  • Supporting document control and appropriate record keeping
  • Undertaking People research where required
  • Providing general People Operations support
  • Taking increasing ownership of agreed processes as your capability develops

What We're Looking For

This is a developmental opportunity, but some existing HR knowledge and practical experience is required.

You should have:

  • Previous practical HR / People Operations experience
  • A CIPD Level 3 or Level 5 qualification, completed or currently being studied
  • Understanding of core employment and HR processes
  • Strong administration and organisational skills
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Confidence working with confidential information
  • Good written communication
  • Ability to follow processes and instructions accurately
  • Willingness to ask questions when something is unclear
  • Ability to manage agreed tasks independently
  • Genuine interest in developing a career within HR / People
  • Comfort working within an early-stage environment where processes are still being developed

Experience within technology, FinTech, financial services, startups or another regulated environment would be useful but is not essential.

We are more interested in finding someone with the right HR foundations, judgement, reliability and desire to develop.

Why This Opportunity?

Unlike an HR role within a large established organisation where responsibilities may be limited to one narrow area, this opportunity offers exposure to the development of a People function from an early stage.

You will have the opportunity to:

  • Work directly with experienced senior People leadership
  • Develop practical People Operations experience
  • Gain exposure across recruitment and the employee/consultant lifecycle
  • Learn how People infrastructure is created and scaled
  • Develop experience within an early-stage FinTech environment
  • Take on increasing responsibility as your capability develops

For the right person, this should provide considerably broader exposure than a narrowly defined junior HR position within a large organisation.

Engagement Structure

This is a flexible, fractional engagement of approximately 6–8 hours per week within an early-stage FinTech venture.

It is particularly suited to someone who wants to develop their HR career while participating in the development of a growing organisation alongside other compatible professional or study commitments.

The engagement is structured around participation in the longer-term development and growth of the business rather than a conventional employment package at this stage.

Full details of the participation structure will be discussed with candidates progressing through the process.

Business Analyst

We are seeking a Business Analyst with operational modelling experience to support a provincial clinical information solution program undergoing significant digital health transformation. This role is central to designing and validating a multi-entity operating model that will consolidate and standardize digital health systems across a large public sector health system. The ideal candidate will translate the program vision into a sustainable, province-wide clinical information solution by overseeing the lifecycle of clinical, technical, business, and operational capabilities across shared services and regional health authorities. This is a strategic opportunity to shape how healthcare delivery will be transformed through standardized digital systems and unified patient-centric care.

This position requires someone who can facilitate multi-entity discussions and develop comprehensive operating models to support large-scale healthcare transformation initiatives. The role involves collaborating closely with subject matter experts, clinical and technology stakeholders, and health administrative leaders to conduct assessments, develop frameworks, analyze capabilities, and create models that achieve consensus on sensitive matters such as service delivery options and organizational structure. Responsibilities include supporting end-to-end capability model development, facilitating workshops with provincial leadership to establish guiding principles and decision rights, designing functional distribution of roles and responsibilities across a multi-entity structure, and supporting options analysis for service delivery models. The successful candidate will produce strategic deliverables including approach frameworks, integrated project plans, governance frameworks, stakeholder engagement plans, capability models, and executive communications, while managing concurrent workstreams and monitoring dependencies and progress against plans.

This position is remote with required travel to the work location at least once monthly throughout the engagement.

Qualifications

  • University degree in Business Administration, Health Informatics, Information Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent combination of relevant education and demonstrated professional experience in healthcare or information systems.
  • 10+ years - Canadian healthcare experience with proven track record navigating and managing multi-organizational partnership needs to enable large-scale transformative healthcare and digital health initiatives within provincial, regional, or health network environments.
  • 15+ years - Consulting experience in strategic planning, business planning, and operating model development for complex digital health initiatives, engaging with senior-level executives and interprofessional teams from hospitals, regional health authorities, or government entities.
  • 10+ years - Government and health system management and planning experience providing strategic leadership, expertise, and project or program management to design, implement, and evaluate policies, clinical programs, operations, administrative, and IT infrastructure.

Nice to Have

  • 10+ years - Demonstrated expertise facilitating multi-entity discussions and workshops for large-scale healthcare and digital health initiatives, aligning stakeholder goals with business objectives, and obtaining buy-in and consensus on sensitive subject matters.
  • 8+ years - Demonstrated experience working with or implementing Clinical Information Systems or other IT and digital health projects in Canada in collaboration with diverse stakeholders such as executives, clinicians, IT, privacy and security.
  • 5+ years - Demonstrated experience supporting healthcare operating model development to enable cost-effective, high-quality, and sustainable programs in a matrixed environment.
  • 10+ years - Project or program leadership managing concurrent workstreams of large-scale healthcare and digital health initiatives in a matrixed environment, from initiation to execution to close out, monitoring dependencies and progress, preparing targeted communications for diverse audiences, managing risks and resources, and aligning stakeholder needs with business objectives.
  • 10+ years - Exceptional verbal and written communication skills to convey and facilitate complex and sensitive subject matters to foster collaboration, obtain buy-in and consensus, and influence change to enable healthcare transformation with senior-level stakeholders. Fluency in both official languages is an asset.
